construction.note: This simpler rosette was worked out for Tastir. An earlier attempt associated it with the text of Sandy Kurt’s zellige PDF, but the recorded drawing comparison found a different design.
construction.changes: It must not be described as following Kurt’s wheel instructions. The owner kept it as a separate construction study. A matching historical panel has not been established.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the unit for every length.

steps.text: Draw a circle with centre O through A. Its radius is the unit for the whole pattern.
Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at E, N, W and S. These letters stand for east, north, west and south.

Draw the line through O that halves the angle at O between E and N. Draw the line through O that halves the angle at O between N and W. These lines cross the circle at NE, NW, SW and SE. The circle is now cut into eight equal parts.

Draw a vertical line through E. Draw a vertical line through W. Draw a horizontal line through N. Draw a horizontal line through S. These lines make a square with corners J, K, L and M. Join J, K, L and M to mark the tile that repeats.
Draw a line through each of NE, NW, SW and SE, at 90° to its line from O. With the sides of the square they make an octagon. Join R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7 and R8 with straight lines.
Draw a straight line through O and R1, O and R2, O and R3, and O and R4. The circle is now cut into sixteen.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a straight line through O and R1. Draw a straight line through O and R4. These lines halve two of the eight parts of the circle.

steps.text: Draw a circle with centre R1 through E. It crosses the line from O to R1 at C. Turn this circle and C round O by 45°, seven times.
Draw a straight line through C and the copy of C three places round, counter-clockwise. Turn this line round O by 45°, seven times. The eight lines make the star at the heart of the rosette.

Draw a line through E parallel to the line from O to R3. Draw a line through E parallel to the line from O to R2. Turn these two lines round O by 45°, seven times. Where they cross the lines of the star, they turn into petals.

Mark G, where the upper line through E crosses a line of the star. Mark P, where that line of the star crosses the line from O to NE. Mark H and Q in the same way below the horizontal line. Turn G, P, H and Q round O by 45°, seven times.
Mark X and Y, where the leaning lines through NE cross the right side and the top of the tile. Turn X and Y round O by 90°, three times.

ink.text: Ink each petal from the middle of a side of the octagon to a point of the star. Ink the short lines from the slanting sides out to the edge of the tile.

parts.text: Ink from E through G to P. Ink from E through H to Q. These lines make one petal of the rosette.
Ink the same two lines at each of NE, N, NW, W, SW, S and SE. Tick “Also ink the copies round the centre” to ink them all at once.
Ink from NE to X. Ink from NE to Y. These short lines run out to the edge of the tile.
Ink the same two lines at NW, SW and SE.

pattern.text: Put copies of the tile side by side. Each rosette touches its neighbours point to point. Where four tiles touch, the lines close into an octagon inside a second eight-pointed star.

expect.note: Golden values, in units of OA, computed by the engine and checked for eight-fold symmetry, no slivers, and pieces that exactly fill the tile.
